section4WaiverExpiry.policySketch: Waiver-expiry policy for the THREE integrity-gate waiver kinds in upstream-sync.json (keep-fork / drop-fork / revert-fork), plus a parallel known-red-expiry for the §2 meta-gate. (1) Integrity waivers: add an optional 'expiresAfterSyncs' (int) or 'expiresOn' (ISO date) field to the Waiver interface in upstream-sync-record.ts. collectGitFailures already tracks per-waiver hit counts and already emits a 'matched no finding … stale' NOTE for zero-hit waivers — extend that: a waiver with decision:'keep' and expiry set becomes a FAILURE (not a note) once expired OR once it goes zero-hit for N consecutive recorded syncs, forcing re-adjudication. decision:'drop' waivers (remediation owed) should carry a hard expiry tied to their ticket — an owed waiver that outlives its expiry with no landed fix escalates to failure so debt cannot be parked forever. decision:'pending' waivers (currently 1: packages/client/ui-settings-models/ revert-fork) get the shortest fuse: pending is a not-yet-decided state and must not survive more than one sync round without a keep/drop decision. (2) Known-red expiry (for the future §2 knownRed[] array): each known-red carries a reopenTrigger (semantic, e.g. 'product internationalization') and optionally a review-by date; on expiry the meta-gate flips the entry from silently-accepted to must-re-justify. This is the structural cure for the exact orphan pattern UM-C-GATES fixed reactively (C-class 4 gates orphaned 2026-09-07→2026-09-11).
section4WaiverExpiry.deferReason: §4 defers this session because (a) it requires a SCHEMA CHANGE to two shipped files — the Waiver interface in scripts/upstream-sync-record.ts (804-line git-layer module whose tsc/oxlint/vitest were themselves only validated at apply time) and the gate-coverage manifest — and adding an expiry field changes collectGitFailures failure semantics (note→failure), which needs its own grilling + spec + test round, not a bolt-on to a re-sync session; (b) the meta-gate half is BLOCKED on a prerequisite that does not exist yet: verify-gate-coverage.ts has no knownRed[] concept at all, so 'known-red expiry' has nothing to expire until the §2 known-red schema extension (itself deferred, see §2 patch) lands first; (c) the policy calibration (N-syncs, expiry windows) is a judgment call in the same family as the still-open cadence thresholds and should be graded by a human, whereas §2+§3 are mechanical/measured and safe to land AFK this session. Expiry is a durability refinement, not a correctness gate — the three integrity checks are already sound without it.
